title: Simultaneous bases in finitely many residue-field targets
statement: Let $(D,\mathfrak m)$ be a nonzero commutative ring with unique maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$, let $k=D/\mathfrak m$ be infinite, and let $Q$ be a $D$-module. Let $I$ be a finite set, possibly empty, and let $r\geq0$ be an integer. For each $i\in I$, let $K_i$ be a field equipped with an embedding $k\hookrightarrow K_i$, let $F_i$ be a $K_i$-vector space of dimension $r$ [def-weil-vector-space-dimension], and let $\rho_i:Q\to F_i$ be $D$-linear, where $D$ acts on $F_i$ through $D\to k\hookrightarrow K_i$. Suppose that the $K_i$-linear span of $\rho_i(Q)$ equals $F_i$ for every $i$. Then there exist $y_1,\ldots,y_r\in Q$ such that $\rho_i(y_1),\ldots,\rho_i(y_r)$ is a $K_i$-basis of $F_i$ for every $i\in I$.

source.place: Tag 03C1 (algebra-lemma-semi-local-module-basis-in-submodule), proof, infinite-field linear avoidance and induction, isolated for finitely many linear targets.

proof.text: If $I=\varnothing$, take every $y_j=0$; there are no basis conditions to check. Otherwise construct, for $0\leq t\leq r$, elements $y_1,\ldots,y_t\in Q$ whose images are linearly independent in every $F_i$. For $t=0$ the empty family is independent. Steps 2--4 give the induction step whenever $t<r$.

source.place: Tag 03C1 (algebra-lemma-semi-local-module-basis-in-submodule), proof: infinite-field linear avoidance and induction on the rank; explicit simultaneous-target adaptation.

proof.text: Let $W_i=\operatorname{span}_{K_i}\{\rho_i(y_1),\ldots,\rho_i(y_t)\}$. If $W_i=F_i$, this independent family is a basis, so [def-weil-vector-space-dimension] gives $r=t$, a contradiction. Thus $W_i$ is proper. Since $\rho_i(Q)$ spans $F_i$, some $q_i\in Q$ has $\rho_i(q_i)\notin W_i$: otherwise its entire span would lie in $W_i$. Choose these witnesses for the finite set $I$.

source.place: Tag 03C1 (algebra-lemma-semi-local-module-basis-in-submodule), proof: infinite-field linear avoidance and induction on the rank; explicit simultaneous-target adaptation.

proof.text: Write $\iota_i:k\hookrightarrow K_i$ for the given embedding. On $V=k^I$ define $T_i(c)=\sum_{j\in I}\iota_i(c_j)\rho_i(q_j)$ and $A_i=T_i^{-1}(W_i)$. Each $T_i$ is $k$-linear, viewing $F_i$ as a $k$-space via $\iota_i$, and $W_i$ is closed under these scalars, so $A_i$ is a $k$-subspace. It is proper: the coordinate vector $e_i$ maps to $\rho_i(q_i)\notin W_i$. The coordinate vectors form a finite basis of $V$ (every $c=\sum_jc_je_j$, with unique coefficients). Apply [lem-pc-finite-linear-avoidance] over the infinite field $k$ to obtain $c\in V\setminus\bigcup_{i\in I}A_i$.

source.place: Tag 03C1 (algebra-lemma-semi-local-module-basis-in-submodule), proof: infinite-field linear avoidance and induction on the rank; explicit simultaneous-target adaptation.

proof.text: Lift each $c_j$ through the surjection $D\to D/\mathfrak m=k$ to $d_j\in D$ and set $y_{t+1}=\sum_{j\in I}d_jq_j$. The specified scalar action and $D$-linearity give $\rho_i(y_{t+1})=\sum_j\iota_i(c_j)\rho_i(q_j)=T_i(c)\notin W_i$. In a relation $a\rho_i(y_{t+1})+\sum_{b=1}^ta_b\rho_i(y_b)=0$, a nonzero $a$ would put $\rho_i(y_{t+1})$ in $W_i$ by division by $a$. Hence $a=0$, and the induction hypothesis forces all $a_b=0$. This proves the required independence at $t+1$.

source.place: Tag 03C1 (algebra-lemma-semi-local-module-basis-in-submodule), proof: infinite-field linear avoidance and induction on the rank; explicit simultaneous-target adaptation.

proof.text: At $t=r$, the images are independent in each $F_i$. If their span were proper, choose $v$ outside it. The relation argument of step 4 shows that adjoining $v$ gives $r+1$ independent vectors. Applying [lem-weil-independent-family-card-le-dimension] to the finite-dimensional $K_i$-space $F_i$ gives $r+1\leq\dim_{K_i}F_i=r$, impossible. Thus the images span and are bases, by [def-weil-vector-space-dimension]. This argument also covers $r=0$: a nonzero vector would give an independent family of size one in dimension zero.
